why: This file exists because the first build of this screen was typed from a 900px screenshot
rather than extracted. That produced three fabricated strings and nine wrong type or
geometry values, and every automated check passed. Everything below is what Figma
actually returned, so verify-content.mjs has something to check the page against.
note: A text node whose content is a single space is EMPTY in the design. The in-progress stage card has one. It is recorded, not tidied away.

placeholders.comment: Down to ONE entry. The screen now shows the design system's own sample employees (People, 329:422) rather than names I made up, so every other string is a straight copy of Figma and verify-content holds the page to Figma's exact words. A shorter map is a stronger check: each entry is a place the page is allowed to differ.

divergences.comment: Known, deliberate differences from the Figma design. Listed so they are decisions rather than drift.
divergences.components: Stepper, People, Rectangle Tags and Right arrow are from a non-People-First library (F-018). The rebuild substitutes People First equivalents where they exist and declares a gap where they do not.
divergences.tags: Figma uses Rectangle Tags with alpha fills (rgba(81,122,56,0.05)). The rebuild uses the People First Tags component.
divergences.personName12px: 12px is not on the People First type ramp (13 / 16 / 20 / 24 / 36). Recorded as a gap; the rebuild uses the 13px label class and this file records the real value.
divergences.emptyTitleHeight: Figma's stage title row is a fixed 22px. On the in-progress card the title is empty, so the prototype keeps the 22px with .stage-title{min-height:22px} — without it the card loses height and the two stages stop lining up. The emptiness is the design; the height keeps it honest.
divergences.buttonCase: Figma draws Close case 13px Regular UPPERCASE with no icon. .pf-button is 13px SemiBold sentence case with a leading icon slot. The library component wins and the icon is dropped, so the page reads 'Close case', not 'CLOSE CASE'. This is the one visible difference from the Figma render.
divergences.cardsAreLocalCss: The header and subject are plain Figma FRAMES, and the stage card is `Clickable card` from a non-People-First library. None is the People First Card, so they are built in local CSS to Figma's measured values and asserted by the `frame` block above. `.pf-card` used to stand in for them at radius 8 / padding 20, which made every screen about a fifth taller than the design.

icons.comment: Sizes as Figma draws them. The 'circle' the case icon sits in is the icon's own outline — assets/icons/case-management.svg is the same speech-bubble ring, and at 28px it stopped reading as one. The defect was the size, not a missing container.

frame_comment: Machine-readable geometry, read by scripts/verify-frame.mjs. Every value is from the saved extract in dsskill/runs/. These frames are NOT the People First Card: the header and subject are plain Figma frames (page layout), and the stage card is `Clickable card` from a non-People-First library (F-018). They are built in local CSS as declared GAPs — and this block is what makes that checkable rather than merely declared.
